title.narrative: Output 2.1. Increased capacity of the member States to ratify international labour standards

description.narrative: Fiji ratified P 155 and C 190 on 25 June 2020. Through the RBSA Project, the ILO was able to technically support Fiji and fund awareness raising workshops to the tripartite partners. The ILO organized information sessions and developed promotion materials on selected ILO conventions (knowledge products). It focused its efforts on the ratification of C190, C160, C161, C162, C187 and P29. It also provided technical assistance through gap analyses to assess the compliance of national legislation with several conventions such as C 190, P 155, and C 160.

description.narrative:
In December 2020, the National Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board (NOSHAB), which is a tripartite mechanism, met a few times to discuss and approve the ratification of C161, C162, and C187.
The Tripartite constituents also participated in tripartite technical meetings and consultations on the implementation of C87, C98, C108, C155, C184, MLC, 2006, C100, C111, C105, C138, C182 and the CEACR's comments on these Conventions. Moreover, they participated in tripartite consultations and meetings for the planning, implementation, and validation of the reports on the following Conventions on C 87, C 155, C182, and the MLC, 2006.
The Fiji Government submitted all newly adopted instruments to Parliament on 22 March 2021 (all pending instruments for the period from 1996 to 2019). The Director General was informed of the submission in May 2021.
The ILO technically supported Fiji through the capacity building of its tripartite constituents with the contribution of RBSA funding.
The ILO advocated for ratification, organised awareness raising sessions and provided technical assistance to Fiji to prepare for the ratification of C161, C162 and C187. At the Government (MEPIR)'s request, the ILO provided its expertise to develop Fiji's National OHS Profile and Fiji's National OHS Policy. After completion of the policy, the development of Fiji's National Chemical Inventory is being planned with support by the Office. The ILO further provided expertise to support the MEPIR to prepare Cabinet papers on the three above-mentioned Conventions.
Based on discussions conducted in December 2020 in the NOSHAB, the tripartite constituents continued their work on the ratification of C161, C162 and C187, which is planned by the end of 2021. Tripartite consultations within the NOSHAB on C160 are also planned by the end of 2021.
The recommendations of the CEACR on the following ratified ILO Conventions were discussed with tripartite constituents on C87, C98, C108, C155, C184, MLC, 2006, C100, C111, C105, C138, C182. The Office prepared guiding notes for the implementation of the CEACR recommendations which are currently being used by the Government for the development of draft amendment Acts and for modified policies and practices.
In August-September 2021, the Office organized a capacity-building event to strengthen the capacities of the tripartite constituents on international labour standards, and the FPRW in line with C144, and COVID responses. Lessons learnt have been shared within the sub region. The aim of the capacity building event was to share knowledge across Pacific island countries (PICs) and to ensure that, other PICs including Fiji can benefit from much needed assistance in the area of ILS in a cost-efficient manner. description.narrative: The Fiji Government submitted eight reports due in 2021 (C29, C105, C122, C138, C142, C 152, C159, C181, and C182). The Office received them within the deadline of 1st of September 2021. The ILO organised a number of awareness raising sessions for the Ministry of Employment, Productivity and Industrial Relations (MEPIR) and the Fiji Trades Union Congress (FTUC) on International Labour Standards (ILS) and reporting. Furthermore, it conducted numerous meetings and consultations with the MEPIR to discuss the reporting details, develop an action plan to prepare reports within the deadline. . To this end, in May 2021, the ILO provided expertise to support the MEPIR to prepare reports due in 2021, discuss them with tripartite constituents, amend and finalise them based on the results of the consultations. The Office also organized an ILS Reporting Course from 22 March 2021 to 14 May 2021, which was attended by two Fiji officials. Six officials from Fiji also benefited from training on ILS and reporting organised specifically for Asia Pacific in August-September 2021.
